name: Disability Tax Credit (DTC)
what: A non-refundable tax credit for people with a severe and prolonged impairment. For a child, approval is the key that unlocks the Child Disability Benefit, the RDSP grants and bonds, and BC's new disability supplement.
amount: 2025 federal disability amount: $10,138, plus a supplement of up to $5,914 for a person under 18 at year-end (CRA, checked 2026-10-14).
who: Child (or adult) has a severe and prolonged impairment in physical or mental functions
A medical practitioner certifies it on Form T2201
steps: Ask your child's doctor, nurse practitioner, psychologist or speech-language pathologist to complete Form T2201 (the CRA has a digital version)
Send it to the CRA using the digital DTC application form or by mail (not through “submit documents”), any time of year
Wait for the CRA's notice of determination
File your taxes every year, even with zero income
docs: Form T2201 (medical part completed by practitioner)
links: Our DTC Playbook: step-by-step, prep sheet, fees, MP help, back pay

name: Child Disability Benefit (CDB)
what: A tax-free monthly payment for families caring for a child under 18 who is approved for the DTC. It is paid with the Canada Child Benefit.
amount: July 2026–June 2027: up to $3,480/year ($290.00/month) per child; reduced when adjusted family net income is over $82,847 (CRA, checked 2026-10-14).
who: You get (or are eligible for) the Canada Child Benefit
Your child is approved for the DTC
steps: Get the DTC approved
If you already get the CCB, the CDB starts automatically; CRA back-pays up to the current and two previous benefit years
File taxes every year (both partners)

name: RDSP, Canada Disability Savings Grant & Bond
what: A long-term savings plan for a person approved for the DTC. The government adds matching grants, and low-income families can get the bond without putting in any money.
amount: Grant: up to $3,500/year, $70,000 lifetime. Bond: up to $1,000/year, $20,000 lifetime, no contribution needed; full bond for 2026 if adjusted family net income is $38,237 or less. When opening a plan you may get up to $11,000 in back bond (canada.ca, checked 2026-10-14).
who: Beneficiary is DTC-approved
Canadian resident with a SIN
Under 60 to open
steps: Get DTC approval
Open an RDSP at a bank or credit union that offers them
Ask them to apply for the grant and bond
Keep filing taxes so the bond keeps coming
docs: SIN for the child and the holder (parent)
links: Canada.ca: How much you could get

name: BC Autism Funding (under 6 / 6–18)
gov: BC (Ministry of Children and Family Development)
what: Funding to pay for autism therapy and supports. IMPORTANT: this program is ending March 31, 2027 and is being replaced by the needs-based BC Children and Youth Disability Benefit and an income-tested Disability Supplement. New applications are open until March 2027.
amount: Under 6: up to $22,000/year per child (RASP professionals, supervised interventionists, family counselling). Ages 6–18: up to $6,000/year per child; up to 20% can go to training, travel and equipment. New Disability Benefit: $6,500 or up to $17,000/year by need; Disability Supplement: up to $6,000/year by income, first payments July 2027 (gov.bc.ca, checked 2026-10-14).
who: BC resident child under 19 with an autism diagnosis from a qualified assessment
For the new Disability Benefit: based on support needs, any diagnosis
steps: Get a diagnosis (public BC Autism Assessment Network or private)
Submit the Autism Funding application and diagnosis to MCFD
Choose providers from the Registry of Autism Service Providers (RASP)
Watch for a ministry letter about moving to the Disability Benefit
links: gov.bc.ca: How much funding is available
gov.bc.ca: Financial supports for children with support needs

name: At Home Program (Medical Benefits)
what: Medical equipment, supplies, orthotics, audiology, dental/optical, therapies and disability-related medical transportation for children with significant daily-living needs, plus PharmaCare Plan F. (The SAET part is moving to the new Disability Benefit; Medical Benefits remain.)
amount: Items are pre-approved and paid directly; no fixed dollar amount.
who: Age 0–17 (benefits until the end of the month they turn 18)
BC resident on MSP, living at home with a parent/guardian
Assessed dependent in 3 of 4: eating, dressing, toileting, washing (under 3: physician attestation)
steps: Talk to your child's doctor or therapist
Complete the application (form CF2160) with an assessment (Vineland-3, PEDI-CAT or GMFCS)
A regional committee decides; you get a letter
Pilot areas (Prince Rupert/Haida Gwaii, Smithers, Terrace, Kelowna) apply through a Family Connections Centre

name: Jordan's Principle
what: Makes sure First Nations children can get the health, social and educational products, services and supports they need, on or off reserve, without delays over who pays.
amount: Case by case; no fixed amount.
who: First Nations child (under the age of majority) in Canada, as defined by ISC's eligibility criteria
On or off reserve
steps: Call 1-855-JP-CHILD (1-855-572-4453), 24/7, or contact the BC regional focal point / a service coordinator
Get a letter of support from a health or education professional, Elder or Knowledge Keeper
Submit with consent and a cost breakdown
Urgent requests (safety, no food, fleeing violence, etc.): call the line directly
If denied, you can appeal
docs: Letter of support linking the request to the child's need

name: First Nations on- and off-reserve supports
what: On reserve, income assistance and assisted living come from ISC through your band office. Off reserve, First Nations families use BC programs (like PWD and income assistance) plus Jordan's Principle, FNHA health benefits, and Indigenous housing providers.
who: On-reserve residents in financial need (On-reserve Income Assistance)
On-reserve people with disabilities or chronic illness needing non-medical care (Assisted Living)
steps: On reserve: start with your band office social development worker
Off reserve: apply to BC programs through My Self Serve; contact a Friendship Centre or BCANDS for help
Use Jordan's Principle for your child's unmet needs
docs: ID, proof of residence and income

name: BC Persons with Disabilities (PWD) designation
gov: BC (Ministry of Social Development and Poverty Reduction)
what: The designation that gives an adult disability assistance (higher rates and asset limits, transportation support, health supplements). It's for adults, so for a child, plan ahead: start at 17½.
amount: See current BC assistance rate tables on gov.bc.ca.
who: 18 or older (can apply from 17½)
Severe physical or mental impairment expected to last 2+ years
Significantly restricted in daily living activities and needs help
Financially eligible (income and asset test)
steps: Apply for assistance on My Self Serve (or skip if already on assistance)
Ask for the PWD application (HR2883)
Have your doctor/nurse practitioner and an assessor complete their sections
Submit; if denied you can request reconsideration (Disability Alliance BC can help)
docs: ID, SIN, bank and income info

name: Crisis supplements & other assistance supplements
what: If you're on income, disability or hardship assistance and face an unexpected emergency need affecting health or safety (food, shelter, clothing), you may get a crisis supplement. There are also security deposit help, Housing Stability Supplement and health supplements.
amount: Set by BC policy; check the supplements page.
who: Family receiving BC income, disability or hardship assistance
Unexpected expense or item you can't otherwise get, where not having it risks health or safety
steps: Contact the ministry (through My Self Serve, by phone, or at an office) as soon as the emergency happens
Explain the need and why you have no other resources
If denied, you can ask for reconsideration
docs: Receipts, notices, quotes about the emergency
links: gov.bc.ca: Supplements for people on assistance

name: BC Housing Rental Assistance Program (RAP)
what: Monthly help with rent in the private market for low-income working families. Not available at the same time as income or disability assistance (both are shelter subsidies).
amount: Depends on income, rent and family size.
who: Household income $60,000 or less (before tax)
At least one dependent child
Not receiving BC income or disability assistance (exception: Medical Services Only)
steps: Check eligibility on BC Housing's RAP page
Apply online or by paper with income and rent proof
Reapply every year

name: Canada Child Benefit & BC Family Benefit
what: Tax-free monthly payments for families with children under 18, both based on your tax return. Neither is counted as income for BC assistance.
amount: CCB July 2026–June 2027: up to $8,157/year per child under 6 ($679.75/month); see CRA for 6–17. BC Family Benefit July 2026–June 2027: up to $1,750 first child, $1,100 second, $900 each additional (checked 2026-10-14).
who: Live with and care for a child under 18
Resident of Canada (and BC for the Family Benefit)
You and your partner file taxes
steps: Apply for the CCB at birth registration, or through CRA My Account
The BC Family Benefit comes automatically with the CCB
File taxes every year, even with no income
